A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pollen color polymorphism in E.  americanum appears to be maintained by a combination of pollinator preferences and selection against the rare color morph at each population.
we found no effect on pollen performance, but pollinator preferences may be an important component of selection on pollen color.
pollen-color polymorphism in E. Americanum is likely maintained by pollinators, and that the maintenance of variation may depend on the constancy and strength of pollinators' preferences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pollen color can be an ecologically important trait, but that the ecological effects of pollen-color variation may be highly context-dependent.
, although pollen color is often assumed to have important ecological effects, the ecological significance of the trait is often poorly understood.
